High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. The Prin. Secy. Home, Lucknow And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajesh Kumar Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Neeraj Kumar Mishra Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
No one has appeared for respondent no.2 despite notice.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0269 of 2023, under Section 376, 323, 504 IPC & 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Mohanlalganj, District Lucknow.

3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that on 04.06.2023 at about 10 AM when the victim was going towards her agricultural filed, the applicant tried to molest her and committed rape on her;
somehow she could escape by raising a hue and cry.

It was further stated that when she went to Anoop vs State Of U.P. Thru. The Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172138223/
1 complain to the applicant's family, the applicant's family hit her very badly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of the victim was disclosed as 18 years.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that a similar statement was given under Section 161 Cr.P.C., however, changing the stand from the FIR, the actual commission of rape was alleged in the said statement.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., a similar statement was given.

5. In the light of the said, the submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that from the medical report on record, there is no categorical view with regard to the commission of offence of rape.
He further draws my attention to an agreement arrived at in between the victim and the applicant wherein both of them had agreed on being married on being enlarged on bail.
It is argued that the applicant is ready and willing to marry, however, unreasonable demands are being made by the victim family.
The applicant is said to be in custody since 10.06.2023 and even the charge has not been framed till date.
6. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the averments made in the FIR alleging the attempt to commit the offence whereas the statement under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., specifically alleging the commissioner of the offence,
being at variance coupled with the fact that they are not supported by the medical on record and the subsequent affidavits signed by both the parties as also the fact that the age of the victim in the FIR is stated to be 18 years, however, there is no other document on record in line with the requirements under the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder, a case for bail is made out.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Anoop be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
